text:
sam: FYI customer (Olga) reporting persistent 429s during a traffic spike on their Dedicated capacity. They say the pool "didn't scale up fast enough" and requests queue and time out. I have a repro and some logs below, can we triage? :thinking:

anya: Can you paste the customer's request id, region, and the Dedicated config (min/max replicas, warm pool settings)? Also any billing/auth errors in the logs could explain blocked scale-ups.

olga: Here are the key traces from our side (sanitized):
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-8k","prompt":"ping"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2025 15:02:10 GMT
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "scaleup_delay: warmup_probe_throttled - service queueing, will retry", "request_id": "acme-req-5566" }
```
Customer also saw long tail 504s when calls waited for provision. They say warm pool size was 2 but ramping didn't start until after 90s.

liam: Region/cluster? Which Dedicated pool? Any model/container image differences?

sam: Pool: eu-west-1, pool-id: ded-eu-42. Model variant: gpt-lite-8k-quant. Config from customer (copied):
```
minReplicas: 1
maxReplicas: 20
warmPoolSize: 2
probe.initialDelaySeconds: 5
probe.periodSeconds: 10
scale.policy.cooldown: 30s
burstCapacity.enabled: true
```
They also used reserved capacity off (billing: on-demand) — customer tried to increase minReplicas but hit an account lock stating "reserve-capacity required for 3+ min replicas in eu-west-1".

mike: Two likely contributors: 1) preflight/auth/imagepull/backoff preventing new pods from becoming Ready quickly; 2) probe throttling / leader backoff in our autoscaler. Need kube events and attach logs. Also noisy neighbor could be saturating NVMe or network causing longer container startup (image pulls).

sam: Attaching debug traces from control plane around the incident window:
```
[2025-06-04T15:01:12Z] attach-controller: starting attach for pool ded-eu-42, targetReplicas=5
[2025-06-04T15:01:16Z] attach-controller: error attach failed: imagePullBackOff (registry rate-limited)
[2025-06-04T15:01:40Z] auth: token validation failed for account acme-prod - HTTP 401 from registry (rotation in progress)
[2025-06-04T15:02:05Z] autoscaler: probe suppressed due to rate-limit window (warmup probes clipped)
[2025-06-04T15:02:55Z] attach-controller: pod became Ready after image pull retry; scaled replicas now 3
```
So we have image pull + registry auth rotation + probe throttling all aligned with the spike.

ops-bot: [ALERT] sustained queue length > 200 requests for pool ded-eu-42 between 2025-06-04T15:01:00Z and 2025-06-04T15:04:00Z. Pending attaches peaked at 17. CPU utilization on existing nodes remained <50%.

anya: Repro plan I recommend: 1) internal spike test (20 qps sustained for 3 min) against ded-eu-42; 2) temporarily set minReplicas=3 and warmPoolSize=4 on a non-prod clone and run; 3) run parallel image-pull stress (concurrent pulls) to simulate registry backoff. Commands to simulate spike: 
```
# simple concurrency harness (k6 or hey)
hey -z 3m -c 40 -q 20 https://dedicated-eu.acme.example/generate
```
Also capture kube events: `kubectl get events -n redwood-pools --field-selector involvedObject.name=ded-eu-42` and control-plane logs from attach-controller.

sam: Customer tried bumping minReplicas to 3 but got a billing hold:
```
Billing: cannot increase reserved capacity. Account locked: "increase_requires_commitment". Contact billing to enable temporary scaled headroom or emergency override.
```
Customer asked for an emergency override; billing said no overrides in region due to quota commitments. That blocked our ability to keep a warm floor.

olga: Confirming — we requested min=3 as a mitigation, billing refused. We hit 429s before the attach completed. We need a short-term mitigation (allow emergency burst for 5-10m) and a long-term fix. :disappointed:

mike: Short term mitigation options: 1) allow an emergency ephemeral override that consumes overage but requires ticket/audit; 2) enable faster image caching (pre-pull) on nodes where we have spare capacity; 3) reduce probe initialDelay so Ready status faster. Long term: improve probe backoff logic and decouple registry auth rotation from attach path.

anya: I'll open a P1 ticket (ENG-PLATFORM) to: reproduce on a non-prod clone, add better metrics on attach timing, and implement an emergency burst policy (flag gated + audit). Will also loop in Billing/Product for policy on transient overrides.

sam: TODO list I'm doing now: 1) open support ticket linking customer logs + billing hold; 2) run repro with liam+anya on non-prod; 3) ask infra to pre-warm images on nodes if we can; 4) propose emergency override workflow to billing.

liam: For the repro I'll capture: attach-controller traces, registry auth logs, kube events, node disk/network metrics, and autoscaler decision logs. If we see many imagePullBackOffs during spike that's likely the main delay.

olga: Appreciate the help — please keep me posted. We'll hold customer expectations; they asked for a timeline for a mitigation.

sam: I'll update Customer Success and schedule a short call with billing/Product today. Leaving ops checklist in the ticket. :thumbsup:
